entities.name: Phoenician Maritime Trade Network
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: The Phoenicians (c. 1500–300 BCE) created the ancient Mediterranean's most extensive maritime trading network from their city-states of Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos. They traded Tyrian purple dye, cedar, glass, and metalwork across the Mediterranean, founded Carthage, and — most lastingly — invented the alphabet that became the basis for Greek, Latin, Arabic, and all modern Western scripts.
